useCase.name: Record an approved fee reduction, by discretionary concession or by scholarship won on a test

intent.name: fee.concession.record
intent.summary: Record a proposed fee reduction against a student — a concession, a discount, or a scholarship won on a test — with why it is being granted and how long it lasts. One step, and it reduces nothing yet.
routesHere: record a 25% tuition concession for this student, valid to the end of the session

routesHere.text: is bache ki fees mein 25% kami kar do
scholarship record karo, test mein pehla aaya hai
routesHere.gloss: record a scholarship, they came first in the test

routesHere.text: transport fee mein 1000 ki chhoot de do
routesHere.gloss: give a 1000 reduction on the transport fee

routesHere.text: bhai behan wala discount laga do

routesHere: record a hardship concession for the Khan child

routesElsewhere.note: A reduction applies from its effective date onward and never recalculates an invoice already issued (BR-8). A bill already raised is corrected another way.
A reduction is withdrawn rather than deleted, with its own reason (BR-10).

request.text: family ko bata do kyun kami di
request.gloss: tell the family why the reduction was given

routesElsewhere.note: The reason recorded is not shown to the family — it may concern their circumstances (BR-12).

request.text: poori class ki fees kam kar do

routesElsewhere.note: A change for everybody is a change to the price list, not a reduction for one student.

steps.note: One step, producing a record at Awaiting approval. A reduction recorded by Accounts alone bills nobody (BR-1) — nothing is reduced until it is approved.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A missing reason, a missing end date, a value above the fee it reduces, a second reduction on the same fee type, a scholarship with no test and a start before the session begins are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the reduction with its value, its scope, its reason and its validity, together with the audit entry or not at all. Nothing is reduced, no invoice changes and the family is told nothing. Approving it is a separate act — and who approves depends on the type (BR-3).

operations.name: fee.concession.record
operations.idempotencyKey: student_id + applies_to + valid_from, since a student holds one reduction per fee type at a time (BR-11)
operations.purpose: Record a proposed reduction against a student, with its basis, the fee types it covers and its validity period.

parameters.name: student_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with class and section.

parameters.notes: An enrolled student belonging to a class with an approved fee structure.

parameters.name: type
parameters.notes: What kind of reduction this is. It decides who approves it — a concession or discount goes to the School Admin, a scholarship to the Principal, because it is awarded on merit and is a claim about the student (BR-3).

parameters.name: basis
parameters.notes: How the reduction is expressed.

parameters.name: percentage
parameters.notes: Greater than zero and not more than 100. Required where the basis is Percentage.

parameters.name: fixed_amount
parameters.notes: Greater than zero and not more than the fee it reduces (BR-6, E3). Required where the basis is Fixed amount.

parameters.name: applies_to
parameters.type: enum: All fee types | Tuition only | Selected fee types
parameters.notes: Which fee types the reduction covers. A transport concession must not silently reduce tuition (BR-5).

parameters.name: fee_type_ids
parameters.notes: Required where applies_to is Selected fee types.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: 20 to 1000 characters. Mandatory (BR-2, E1) — a family paying less than their neighbour is a question the school has to be able to answer. Never shown to the family (BR-12).

parameters.name: valid_from
parameters.notes: Not before the academic session start (E8). The reduction applies from here onward.

parameters.name: valid_to
parameters.notes: Mandatory (BR-9, E2). A reduction with no end date runs forever and is never reviewed — a concession granted for one hard year must not still be running five years later.

parameters.name: test_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with date and class.

parameters.notes: The scholarship test the award was won on. Required for a scholarship (E7); the score and rank are carried from the marked result rather than typed (BR-4).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Awaiting approval. Nothing is reduced yet (BR-1).

fields.name: approver_role
fields.description: School Admin for a concession or discount; Principal for a scholarship (BR-3).

fields.name: score
fields.description: Carried from the marked test result, never typed (BR-4). Scholarships only.

fields.name: existing_reductions
fields.description: Any reduction the student already holds, and on which fee types — two on the same type is refused (BR-11, E6).

fields.name: recorded_by
fields.description: The acting user, who may not also approve it (BR-1).

errors.note: Message: "Write why this reduction is being granted." Ask; never compose one.
A reduction with no end runs forever and is never reviewed (BR-9).

errors.meaning: The reduction is more than the fee it reduces.
errors.note: There is no route by which a concession pays a family (BR-6). The message names the fee.

errors.meaning: The student already holds a reduction on that fee type.
errors.note: A student may hold several reductions provided they cover different fee types (BR-11). The message names the existing one.

errors.meaning: A scholarship was recorded with no test.
errors.note: A scholarship carries the test and score it was won on, so a discretionary favour and an earned award are not confused (BR-4).

errors.meaning: The validity start is before the academic session begins.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. A family paying less than their neighbour is a question the school has to be able to answer (BR-2), and the reason is the answer. It is never shown to the family either (BR-12), so it can say what it needs to.

Never supply the end date. A reduction with no end runs forever and is never reviewed (BR-9), and how long a family's circumstances warrant it is a judgement somebody makes — not a default of one session.
Never widen applies_to. A transport concession must not silently reduce tuition (BR-5), and "All fee types" chosen because the request was vague reduces charges nobody discussed.
Never type a scholarship's score. It is carried from the marked test result (BR-4), and typing it is how a discretionary favour gets recorded as an earned award.

Choose the type from what the actor said, not from the value. The type decides who approves it — a scholarship goes to the Principal because it is a claim about the student's merit (BR-3) — so calling a hardship concession a scholarship routes it past the wrong person.
Never chain the approval. A reduction recorded by Accounts alone bills nobody (BR-1), and that is the control.
Never offer to reduce an invoice already issued. A reduction applies from its effective date onward and never recalculates one (BR-8).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A recorded reduction is approved, returned or withdrawn — never deleted. The record of what a family was granted survives (BR-10). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, academic session 2025-26 running to 30-06-2027.

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, where the student already holds a tuition concession.

steps.note: Permitted: a student may hold several reductions provided they cover different fee types (BR-11). Naming Transport specifically is what keeps them apart (PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: A second record at Awaiting approval, covering transport only. Had it named tuition, E6 would have refused it — two reductions on one fee type is not allowed.

intent.name: fee.concession.approve
intent.summary: Approve a fee reduction so it applies to every subsequent invoice. School Admin for a concession or discount; Principal for a scholarship. One step.
routesHere: approve the concession for this student
sign off the reduction Accounts recorded

request.text: purane bill bhi kam kar do

routesElsewhere.note: A reduction never recalculates an invoice already issued (BR-8).

steps.note: One step. From here the reduction is applied automatically to every subsequent invoice — nobody remembers to apply it, and nobody can forget (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The acting role against the reduction's type is enforced by the API and arrives as an error — a School Admin cannot approve a scholarship (BR-3, E5).
plan.atomicity: One write: the approval and the audit entry together or not at all. Nothing is billed by it. From the effective date onward every invoice raised for the student carries the reduction automatically (BR-7), and no invoice already issued is recalculated (BR-8). The reduction is surfaced for review when its end date is reached (BR-9). The reason stays internal (BR-12).

operations.name: fee.concession.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: concession_id, since a reduction carries one approval
operations.purpose: Approve a reduction so it applies automatically to every subsequent invoice.

parameters.name: concession_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No reduction matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, type, value, fee types covered and status.

parameters.notes: The reduction, resolved from how the actor named it — the student, the type, or the reference.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: approved_by
fields.description: The School Admin, or the Principal for a scholarship (BR-3).

fields.name: valid_to
fields.description: When it is surfaced for review (BR-9).

fields.name: invoices_recalculated
fields.description: Always zero. A reduction never recalculates an issued invoice (BR-8).

errors.meaning: Accounts attempted to approve their own reduction.
errors.note: Reducing what a family pays is not one person's decision (BR-1).

errors.meaning: A School Admin attempted to approve a scholarship.
errors.note: A scholarship is awarded on merit and is a claim about the student, so the Principal approves it (BR-3).

errors.meaning: An invoice was issued before the reduction was approved.
errors.note: Report it — the family's current bill does not carry the reduction and they will ask why.

planningRules.rule: Never approve a scholarship in a School Admin's session. E5 is BR-3 working — a scholarship is a claim about the student's merit and the Principal makes it.
Report what the next invoice will be reduced by. The office answers the family from it, and a reduction approved silently is one nobody can explain at the counter.
Report where an invoice was issued before approval. It is not recalculated (BR-8, E9), so the family's current bill is the full amount and they will ask why — better said now than at the bank.
Never quote the reason to the family. It may concern their circumstances, and a parent reading the school's assessment of their finances helps nobody (BR-12).
Report the end date. The reduction is surfaced for review when it is reached (BR-9), and a family should know it is not permanent.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An approval is not withdrawn by reversal. A reduction is withdrawn through fee.concession.withdraw, with its own reason, and the record of what the family was granted survives (BR-10). Invoices already reduced under it are not re-billed. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

operations.name: fee.concession.return
operations.purpose: Send a proposed reduction back to Accounts with the reason it was not approved.

parameters.name: concession_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No reduction matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, type, value, fee types covered and status.

parameters.notes: The reduction, resolved from how the actor named it — the student, the type, or the reference.

parameters.name: return_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required. The approver's own words — Accounts have to know whether the value, the scope, the validity or the justification is the problem.

parameters.name: branch_id

errors.meaning: A return was recorded with no reason.
The acting user recorded it themselves.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the return reason. Accounts have to know whether the value, the scope, the validity or the justification is the problem, and only the approver can say.
Never adjust the reduction on the approver's behalf. Changing a percentage or a fee type is Accounts' work in their own session; returning states what is wrong.
Report that nothing has been reduced. The student is being billed in full and will continue to be.

intent.name: fee.concession.withdraw
intent.summary: Withdraw an approved reduction before its end date, with the reason. One step, and it leaves the record of what was granted.

Invoices already reduced under the concession are not re-billed. It applies from its date onward, in both directions (BR-8).

steps.note: One step. The reduction is withdrawn rather than deleted, and the withdrawal carries its own reason — the record of what a family was granted survives (BR-10).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The reason is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.

operations.name: fee.concession.withdraw
operations.idempotencyKey: concession_id, since a reduction is withdrawn once and Withdrawn is terminal
operations.purpose: Withdraw an approved reduction, keeping the record of what was granted and why.

parameters.name: concession_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No reduction matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, type, value, fee types covered and status.

parameters.notes: The reduction, resolved from how the actor named it — the student, the type, or the reference.

parameters.name: withdrawal_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required (BR-10). The actor's own words — a family whose reduction stops will ask, and this is the answer.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: withdrawal_reason
fields.description: As given, kept with the record (BR-10).

fields.name: invoices_affected
fields.description: Always zero. Invoices already reduced are not re-billed (BR-8).

fields.name: next_invoice_effect
fields.description: What the student's next bill will be without it, so the office can answer the family.

fields.name: family_notified
fields.description: Whether the family is told. The reason is not shown to them (BR-12).

errors.meaning: A withdrawal was attempted with no reason.
errors.note: Ask; never compose one. The record of what a family was granted has to say why it stopped (BR-10).

planningRules.rule: Never compose the withdrawal reason. A family whose reduction stops will ask why, and BR-10 keeps the reason with the record precisely so somebody can answer.
Never offer to re-bill invoices already reduced. The reduction applied while it was live and those bills stand (BR-8) — withdrawing it changes what comes next, not what has gone.
Report what the next invoice will be. A family used to paying a reduced amount will receive a full bill, and the office should be able to explain it before they ring.
Never quote the reason to the family. It may concern their circumstances (BR-12), and this one especially — a reduction withdrawn because circumstances improved is not something to put in a message.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Withdrawn is terminal. Where the reduction should resume, a fresh one is recorded and approved on its own merits — and the earlier one and its withdrawal both stay on the record (BR-10). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.
